title: Inverse Trigonometric Functions
seo_title: Inverse Trig Functions Worksheet: arcsin, arccos, arctan | 100 Questions with Answers
standard_text: Understand that restricting a trigonometric function to a domain on which it is always increasing or always decreasing allows its inverse to be constructed.
meta_desc: Free precalculus worksheet on inverse trigonometric functions: exact values, domain and range, compositions, calculator values and angle word problems. 100 questions.
key_big: sin⁻¹ x is the angle whose sine is x, taken from a fixed range.
key_sub: sin⁻¹ and tan⁻¹: −π/2 to π/2. cos⁻¹: 0 to π.
body_html:
How it works

  • sin⁻¹ x (also arcsin x) is the angle whose sine is x. It is not 1/sin x.
  • Each inverse gives one angle from a fixed range: sin⁻¹ and tan⁻¹ from −π/2 to π/2, cos⁻¹ from 0 to π.
  • The domain of sin⁻¹ and cos⁻¹ is −1 ≤ x ≤ 1. tan⁻¹ takes every real number.
  • For cos(sin⁻¹ x) and similar, draw a right triangle for the inner angle and read the outer ratio.
Example

Find cos⁻¹(−12).

The range is 0 to π

cos(2π/3) = −1/2

Answer: 2π3

Example

Find sin⁻¹(sin 5π6).

sin(5π/6) = 1/2

The angle in −π/2 to π/2 with sine 1/2 is π/6

Answer: π6

Example

Find tan(cos⁻¹ 35).

Adjacent 3, hypotenuse 5, so opposite 4

tan = 4/3

Answer: 43

Common mistakes

  • Giving an angle outside the range, such as 5π/6 for sin⁻¹(1/2).
  • Reading sin⁻¹ x as 1/sin x.
  • Using cos⁻¹ when the sides are opposite and hypotenuse. Match the inverse to the sides you know.
  • Leaving the calculator in the wrong mode (degrees or radians).

faq.q: What is the difference between sin⁻¹ x and 1/sin x?
faq.a: sin⁻¹ x is the inverse function: the angle whose sine is x. 1/sin x is the reciprocal, csc x.

faq.q: What are the ranges of the inverse trig functions?
faq.a: sin⁻¹ and tan⁻¹ give angles from −π/2 to π/2 (−90° to 90°); cos⁻¹ gives angles from 0 to π (0° to 180°).
Because 5π/6 is outside the range of sin⁻¹. The answer is the angle in the range with the same sine, π/6.

faq.q: How do you find cos(sin⁻¹ x)?
faq.a: Draw a right triangle with an angle whose sine is x, find the missing side with the Pythagorean theorem and read off the cosine.

items.q: Why must the domain of sine be restricted to define sin⁻¹?
c: Sine is undefined for some angles
Sine is not one-to-one, so it needs a piece where each output happens once
items.e: A function needs exactly one output for each input, so the inverse needs a one-to-one piece. Sine is not one-to-one, so it needs a piece where each output happens once.

items.q: A plane is 2,000 ft above the ground and 10,000 ft (horizontally) from the start of the runway. To the nearest degree, what is the angle of depression from the plane to the runway?
items.e: θ = tan⁻¹(2,000/10,000) ≈ 11°. The angle of depression equals the angle of elevation from the runway.

items.q: A road sign says the grade is 8%: the road rises 8 ft for every 100 ft horizontally. To the nearest tenth of a degree, what angle does the road make with the horizontal?
items.e: θ = tan⁻¹(8/100) ≈ 4.6°. A 8% grade is not 8°.

items.q: A ramp rises 3 ft over a horizontal distance of 24 ft. To the nearest tenth of a degree, what angle does the ramp make with the ground?
items.e: Rise is opposite and run is adjacent: θ = tan⁻¹(3/24) ≈ 7.1°.

items.q: A 30-ft pole casts a 4-ft shadow. To the nearest degree, what is the angle of elevation of the sun?
